title: Wall washing
audience: Cleaners who wash painted or sealed walls, skirting boards and surrounds in any cleaning-group business.
learningOutcomes: Cover every electrical socket and switch with masking tape before the wall is wet.
Dust the wall from the bottom up, including the skirting board, before washing.
Apply product to the cloth rather than the wall, and wash bottom to top in figure-of-eight passes.
Rinse and remove product from top to bottom, so that no run marks are left.
Recognise when a wall is out of safe reach and stop for suitable access equipment.

instruction.heading: Why walls need a fixed method
instruction.body: Walls collect dust, fingerprints and splashes, and the build-up is usually heaviest in a band near the floor. Done carelessly, wall washing leaves run marks, lets liquid reach electrical fittings, and sprays product onto furniture and the customer. A fixed sequence (protect, dust, apply, wash, rinse, check) keeps the wall, the fittings and the people nearby safe. The source emphasises that the customer's property should not be damaged, and that neither the property nor the customer should be sprayed with chemicals.

instruction.heading: Protecting the wall, the floor and the fittings
instruction.body: Before any product touches the wall, cover every electrical socket and switch with masking tape, working from the bottom up. Place plastic sheeting under the bucket to protect carpet or flooring. Move furniture where you can, and get the client's agreement for anything that cannot be moved. When the work is finished, remove the tape with dry hands only, because wet hands near a socket are an electrical hazard.

instruction.heading: Dusting, applying and washing
instruction.body: Dust the wall from the bottom up, including the skirting board, to remove loose material before any liquid is used. Apply the diluted product to your cloth rather than spraying the wall, because spray causes overspray onto people and nearby items. Wash in figure-of-eight passes from the bottom of the wall to the top. The lower band is usually dirtier and needs longer contact time, so reapply product to the cloth where the lower band needs it.

instruction.heading: Rinsing and checking the result
instruction.body: Remove the product with clean water and a clean cloth, working from top to bottom in figure-of-eight passes, so that drips run into areas you have already rinsed. Rinse the cloth often. A finished wall has no run marks, and the skirting board is clean and free of dust. Check each section of wall in good light before you move on.

instruction.heading: Walls out of safe reach
instruction.body: If a wall is higher than you can reach safely from the floor, stop. Do not stretch, lean or stand on furniture. Use suitable access equipment in line with the site's work-at-height rules, or arrange another method with the supervisor. This lesson does not cover height work. The window and exterior lessons carry their own rules for that work.

procedure: Check the product SDS and dilution, and confirm the wall can be reached safely from the floor.
Tape over every electrical socket and switch, working from the bottom up.
Place plastic sheeting under the bucket and protect the carpet or flooring.
Dust the wall from the bottom up, including the skirting board.
Apply the diluted product to the cloth, not the wall. Wash bottom to top in figure-of-eight passes.
Reapply product to the cloth as needed, especially for the lower band.
Rinse with clean water and a clean cloth, top to bottom in figure-of-eight passes.
Remove the tape with dry hands, check for run marks, wash the equipment thoroughly, and store it by colour.

workedExamples.situation: A hallway wall has a dirty lower band and a double power point half-way up. The client asks you to wash the wall quickly.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which steps are essential before the cloth touches the wall?
workedExamples.reasoning: Tape the double power point first, from the bottom up. Put plastic sheeting under the bucket to protect the carpet, and dust the wall, including the skirting board. Only then apply the product to the cloth. The lower band may need a second pass with fresh product. Never spray product near the socket area.

workedExamples.situation: A wall in a commercial foyer is above your safe reach from the floor.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Do not stretch, lean, or stand on furniture, and tell your supervisor. Arrange suitable access equipment under the site's work-at-height rules, or agree another method. This lesson does not authorise height work.

equipmentAndPpe: Eye protection where splash or overspray is possible.
Masking tape for sockets and switches.
Plastic sheeting for the bucket area.
Dusting tools and clean cloths, colour coded.
Access equipment only where authorised and suitable for the task.

commonErrors.error: Spraying product straight onto the wall.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply product to the cloth, then wipe the wall.

commonErrors.error: Wet washing with the sockets untaped.
commonErrors.prevention: Tape every socket and switch before any liquid is used.

commonErrors.error: Washing top to bottom, which lets dirty drips run into the lower band.
commonErrors.prevention: Wash bottom to top, and rinse top to bottom.
Dry hands only for tape removal.

commonErrors.error: Standing on furniture to reach higher.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, and use authorised access equipment or another method.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical hazard: every socket and switch is taped before wet work, and the tape is removed with dry hands only.
This lesson does not authorise height work.
Chemical use follows “Chemical competency: reading labels and safety data sheets”: check the SDS, dilute to the label and do not mix products.
Slip hazard: water running onto floors must be dried and signposted while wet.

qualityStandard: Every socket and switch taped before wet work, and the tape removed afterwards.
Wall dusted from the bottom up, including the skirting board, before washing.
No run marks visible after rinsing.
Skirting board clean and free of dust.
No product spray on furniture, floor or people.
documentationEvidence: Pre-task record of the walls, fixtures and any client instruction.
Record of any damage, marks or defects on the wall found before work started.
summary: Tape the sockets, cover the floor, then dust before any liquid is used.
Product goes on the cloth, not the wall. Wash bottom to top; rinse top to bottom.
Remove tape with dry hands only.
A wall out of safe reach is a stop point, not a reason to stretch.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before wet washing a wall, what must be done to the electrical sockets?
options: Nothing, if they are switched off at the wall socket
Cover them with masking tape, working from the bottom up
Spray them with water to keep the dust down before you begin

knowledgeChecks.question: Which direction is the wall washed, and which direction is it rinsed?
options: Wash bottom to top, rinse top to bottom
Wash top to bottom, rinse bottom to top
Wash and rinse both from the middle outward

knowledgeChecks.question: A wall is above your safe reach from the floor. What is the right response?
options: Stand on a chair and reach across, keeping your balance
Stop and use suitable access equipment, or ask for another method
Lean further out from the floor so the cloth reaches
